title: Adding a cafe, drinks or events to a glass studio: health department food permit and plan review, temporary event permits, meals tax, ABC licence pointers and the City's assembly and special event rules
question: My glass studio will have a small cafe, serve drinks at sip-and-blow events, and host classes and parties. What health, meals tax, alcohol, fire and event approvals does that add in Charlottesville?
office: Blue Ridge Health District, Charlottesville/Albemarle Environmental Health office (Virginia Department of Health food establishment permits); Commissioner of the Revenue (meals tax); Virginia ABC (alcohol licences, state); Charlottesville Fire Marshal's Office (assembly and open-flame permits); NDS Zoning (temporary use permits); Parks & Recreation (special events on City property)
summary: Serving food or drink to the public makes the studio a food establishment under Virginia law and needs a Virginia Department of Health permit from the Blue Ridge Health District's Charlottesville/Albemarle office (1138 Rose Hill Drive, 434-972-6219, CAHDEH@vdh.virginia.gov). The district's process starts before construction: a commercial plan review ($40 statewide; the district page quotes an $80 application fee), submitted with the building permit and business license applications at least 30 days before opening or renovation, then plan approval, a pre-opening inspection (which requires the City's occupancy permit and a Certified Food Protection Manager on site), and the permit, posted where customers can see it. Food at a one-off event needs a Temporary Food Establishment permit ($40, applied for at least 10 days ahead) unless the studio already holds a permanent permit and tells the district. A cafe is a 'General food and beverage' use under the Development Code, permitted in the same districts as an artisan workshop; events are 'General indoor entertainment and recreation' (event venue) indoors, or a $250 Temporary Use Permit for outdoor assemblies on the lot (9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, at most 5 a year). The City's 7% meals tax applies to all prepared food and drink, registered with the Commissioner of the Revenue and filed by the 20th of each month. Alcohol needs a Virginia ABC retail licence (state); the Development Code allows a food and beverage or entertainment use to serve alcohol only as an accessory use. The Fire Marshal's Office may require operational permits for a place of assembly, open flames in assembly or dining areas, and commercial cooking, and a Type 1 kitchen hood needs its own building permit. Events on City streets or property go through Parks & Recreation's special event permit ($25, 30 or 60 days ahead; tents over 900 square feet need a tent permit).

steps.step: Decide what you will serve: that sets which permits apply
steps.how: VDH exempts vendors that offer only non-TCS pre-packaged foods (no eggs, dairy, meat or other foods needing temperature control), so a studio that sells only sealed snacks and canned or bottled drinks may need no food permit; ask the Blue Ridge Health District to confirm. Preparing coffee drinks, food or opening and pouring drinks for the public makes it a food establishment needing a permit. Alcohol of any kind needs a Virginia ABC licence (state), and the Development Code allows a cafe or event venue to serve alcohol only as an accessory use. Each choice also triggers the City's meals tax, the Fire Marshal's permits, and a Type 1 hood if there is grease-producing cooking.
steps.quote: The following individuals or organizations are exempt from the requirement to obtain a VDH Food Permit before serving food to the public.

steps.step: Check the zoning for the cafe and events
steps.how: A cafe is 'General food and beverage' (up to 4,000 SF): permitted by right in RX-3 and RX-5 with use standards and in all CX, NX, DX and IX districts and CM. An indoor event space is 'General indoor entertainment and recreation' (event venue), by right up to 4,000 SF in the CX, NX, DX and IX districts and CM, and by Special Use Permit in CV. Ask Zoning whether occasional classes-with-drinks and private parties are accessory to the artisan workshop or a second principal use. Outdoor events on the lot need a Temporary Use Permit under Development Code Div. 3.6 ($250; up to 5 per year, 21 days apart; outdoor assemblies 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM with parking of one space per 4 persons, meeting the building and fire codes; the Administrator may require a bond). See glass_studio_zoning_use.
steps.fee: Temporary Use Permit: $250 ($500 after the fact)
steps.quote: A temporary use or structure for one or more of the uses described in this Division must obtain a temporary use permit pursuant to 5.2.10. Permit Review.

steps.step: Apply to the Blue Ridge Health District for plan review before building the cafe
steps.who: Operator; Blue Ridge Health District, Charlottesville/Albemarle Environmental Health office
steps.how: Whenever a food establishment is constructed, remodeled or converted from another use, plans must go to the health department before work starts, and construction cannot begin until the commercial plan review is done. The district's steps: start the building permit application with the City building official; apply for the City business license; then file the Plan Review Application and the Application for Foodservice Establishment Permit with the Environmental Health office for the locality (for Charlottesville, 1138 Rose Hill Drive). The district page states an $80 application fee; the statewide VDH page describes a $40 plan review fee and a $40 permit fee, and the district's fee schedule lists Food Service Plan Review $40 and the annual permit $40. Submit scaled floor plans showing all fixed equipment and plumbing, equipment specification sheets, a site plan (dumpsters, grease interceptor), the proposed menu, the projected meals per day and the Certified Food Protection Manager's credentials. The owner of record must apply at least 30 days before opening or the start of renovation.
steps.deadline: At least 30 days before opening to the public or the start of renovation; before construction begins
steps.fee: $80 application fee (district page); plan review $40 and annual permit $40 (district fee schedule and statewide VDH page)

steps.step: Answer the plan review letter, build, then schedule the pre-opening inspection
steps.who: Operator; the district's Environmental Health Specialist
steps.how: The district sends a letter listing any changes and approving the plans for construction; reply in writing on how you will comply. When construction is finished and equipment is in place, call the specialist at least 3 days ahead to schedule the pre-opening inspection. For approval you must show the Occupancy Permit issued by the City building official, have a person in charge with a current Food Safety Manager certification, refrigerators at 41°F or lower and freezers at 0°F or lower with thermometers, a clean facility and a final menu. No food may be served to the public before the inspection passes and the permit is issued. The permit is mailed within 5 to 7 days and must be posted where customers can see it. The permit is annual ($40) and inspections are unannounced.
steps.deadline: Call at least 3 days before the inspection date you want
steps.quote: No food can be served to the public prior to the pre-opening inspection and approval by the Health Department permit has been issued.

steps.step: For food at a one-off event: Temporary Food Establishment permit, or notify the district if you already hold a permit
steps.who: Operator (and the event coordinator, if someone else runs the event); Blue Ridge Health District
steps.how: A Temporary Food Establishment operates for up to 14 consecutive days with a single event. Submit the Temporary Food Establishment Permit Application and Screening Questions with the $40 fee to the local Environmental Health office at least 10 calendar days before the event; the specialist inspects on site before issuing the permit, which must be posted and is valid only for the stated period. An event coordinator should file the Temporary Event Coordinator Application at least 10 days ahead with the vendor list, layout, toilets, waste disposal and water supply. If the studio already holds a permanent VDH permit and prepares the food as its approved plans allow, no extra permit is needed, but the district must know you will operate at the event and the permit must be posted there. Since July 1, 2023 the person in charge of any food establishment, including a TFE, must be a Certified Food Protection Manager unless exempt.
steps.deadline: Application and fee at least 10 calendar days before the event
steps.fee: $40 per Temporary Food Establishment permit (no fee for qualifying nonprofit organizations)
steps.quote: The completed application and fee must be received at a minimum of (10) days prior to the event.

steps.step: Register for the City meals tax and file monthly
steps.how: Add the 7% City meals tax to all prepared food and drink, including alcoholic drinks, on top of the 5.3% Virginia sales tax. Register by filing the Meals Tax Registration with the Business License Application and a copy of the health permit or inspection, through the Secure Portal (category 'Food & Beverage (Meals) Tax Registration / Tax Return') or by mail to PO Box 2964. File and pay by the 20th of each month in the Business Tax Portal, even for months with no sales; a 3% seller's discount applies when filed and paid on time. Details, exemptions and penalties are in meals_tax_filing.json.
steps.deadline: Monthly, by the 20th of the following month

steps.step: If you will serve alcohol: get a Virginia ABC retail licence (state) and check the local rules
steps.who: Operator; Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority
steps.how: Alcohol licensing is a state process not modeled here. Va. Code § 4.1-206.3 lists the retail licences: a mixed beverage restaurant licence requires a restaurant that meets the food-to-beverage ratio and brings with it the right to a wine and beer licence; on-and-off-premises wine and beer licences go to hotels, restaurants and clubs; mixed beverage limited caterer's licences cover up to 12 private gatherings or special events a year for a business regularly providing food and beverages; and per-day event licences exist for events. Apply through Virginia ABC's licensing pages (abc.virginia.gov/licenses) and tell the Commissioner of the Revenue, whose checklist lists ABC licensing. Under the Development Code, a food and beverage or indoor entertainment use may serve alcohol only for on-premise consumption as an accessory use, and a City special event permit can be denied where a required ABC licence has not been obtained.
steps.fee: State and local ABC licence fees (Va. Code § 4.1-233.1 for the local fee; not read)
steps.quote: The granting of a license pursuant to this subdivision shall automatically authorize the licensee to obtain a license to sell and serve wine and beer for on-premises consumption and in closed containers for off-premises consumption; however, the licensee shall be required to pay the local fee required for such additional license pursuant to § 4.1-233.1 .

steps.step: Fire Marshal and building-code items for the cafe and events
steps.who: Operator; Fire Marshal's Office (434-970-3328); NDS Building Inspections
steps.how: Under SFPC Table 107.2 the fire official may require operational permits to operate a place of assembly, to use open flames or candles in assembly or dining areas, and to operate commercial cooking appliances outside assembly occupancies and dwellings; public glassblowing demonstrations are hot work needing a permit. The Fire Marshal's Office lists restaurants, assembly and event spaces and multi-use commercial buildings among the occupancies it inspects, and hood suppression and kitchen hood cleaning reports must be filed through IROL. On the building side a Type 1 commercial kitchen hood has its own permit line ($75 minimum), and the certificate of occupancy will state the occupant load, which the fire code enforces. See glass_studio_fire_permits and glass_studio_building_mechanical.
steps.fee: Commercial Kitchen Hood (Type 1) permit: $75 minimum; fire operational permit fees not published
steps.quote: Places of assembly. An operational permit is required to operate a place of assembly.

steps.step: Events on City streets, sidewalks, parks or the Downtown Mall: Parks & Recreation special event permit
steps.who: Event sponsor; Charlottesville Parks & Recreation (Events Coordinator)
steps.how: Events on City property or needing street closures need a special event permit from Parks & Recreation: a formal application, signed and mailed to Charlottesville Parks & Recreation, P.O. Box 911, with the $25 non-refundable fee, at least 30 days before the event (60 days with a street closure); the Special Event Regulations say 30 or 60 business days and not more than 6 months ahead. The regulations require insurance and indemnification for larger events, say a permit may be denied where a required Health Department or ABC permit has not been obtained, and set the tent rules: tents over 900 square feet need a tent permit from the City Building Code Office in NDS, tents of 400 to 900 square feet are inspected by the Fire Department before use, and pop-up canopies are not allowed on the Downtown Mall. City services are not available during UVA home football games. Vendor stands and outdoor cafe permits on the Mall have their own fees in the NDS schedule.
steps.deadline: Application 30 days before an event without a street closure, 60 days with one (the regulations say business days)
steps.fee: $25 non-refundable application fee; tent permit $50 per tent; street or alley closing $125 (NDS Fee Schedule)
steps.quote: All formal application requests should be completed, signed and mailed to:

caveats: Fees from the Blue Ridge Health District conflict: the new-facility page says 'Application fee: $80', the district fee schedule (effective July 1, 2019) lists plan review $40 and the annual permit $40, and the statewide VDH page describes $40 for plan review and $40 for the permit. $80 may be the two together. Confirm with the Rose Hill Drive office.
Whether a studio that only sells sealed drinks and packaged snacks, or pours wine at a paid class, needs a VDH permit depends on the district's reading of the exemptions; ask before opening.

Virginia ABC licensing is only pointed to. The licence type for drinks at classes and private events (restaurant, limited caterer, or per-day event licence), the food-to-beverage ratio and the local fee under § 4.1-233.1 were not researched; the ABC 'Get a Virginia ABC Retail License' page loaded as a navigation shell without the licence list.

The Development Code allows alcohol only as an accessory use for food and beverage and indoor entertainment uses; whether an artisan workshop may serve alcohol at all (accessory to what?) is a zoning question not answered by the Code text read.

The Parks & Recreation special event permit covers events on City property and street closures; the Special Event Regulations PDF (undated on its face) says 30 or 60 business days while the web page says 30 or 60 days.
Fire Marshal operational permits for assembly, open flames and commercial cooking are listed in the state table; the City does not publish which it requires or at what fee.
The meals tax process is modeled in meals_tax_filing.json; the 7% rate and the 20th-of-the-month deadline are repeated here from the city's Meals Tax page.
